criteria.criterion: A test through locate() on a temp git repo writes the approval where approve-work writes it (records branch) and the rejection where reject-work writes it (current branch, main, via commit_records), and shows both decided proposals absent from the page. Run: cargo test -p xtask decisions.
criteria.evidence: page_with() runs init_repo, puts approvals on the records branch with RecordsWriter::append, commits rejections to main with commit_to_main, then calls render(&locate(dir)). Both new tests assert the decided titles are absent, and both passed. Caveats: commit_to_main is a plain `git commit` to main, not commit_records. xtask cannot call commit_records because it does not depend on athena-core, and the effect on main's tree is the same. Also, crates/athena-core/src/work_decisions.rs:341 shows approve_work writing through self.commit_records to the current branch (main), the same as reject_work at :380. So the criterion's parenthetical 'records branch' is wrong about the code; see findings. Approvals on main are still covered by the existing `proposals_decided_on_main_drop_off_the_page`.

findings.summary: New test doc comment says approve-work writes approvals to the records branch, but it writes to main.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-core/src/work_decisions.rs:341 shows approve_work calling self.commit_records, the same as reject_work at :380. commits.rs:240 shows commit_records committing on top of the current branch. The real approval 20261027-074524-5j98 is in main's records/ in the evidence snapshot. The module doc of the same file also says approve-work records on main, so the comment contradicts it. The claim comes from the accepted reading's criterion 3. Test coverage is not hurt: proposals_decided_on_main_drop_off_the_page still covers approvals on main.
findings.location: xtask/src/decisions.rs page_with() doc comment ("An approval is written where approve-work writes it (the records branch)")

findings.summary: Comment and changelog slightly misstate what fails on the base.
findings.evidence: The comment says proposals_decided_on_main_drop_off_the_page 'passes there too', and the changelog says 'only the within-limit assertions fail on the code before this change'. But the edited assertion `contains("Nothing waiting for you")` (:819, :881, :971) would also fail on the base, whose empty-state text is 'No proposal is waiting for a decision' (from the diff). The behavioral point holds: decided proposals were already dropped. The wording claim does not.

findings.summary: The limit filter reads role definitions only from the records branch.
findings.evidence: Roles are read only under records/roles on athena/records. The evidence shows role records, including steward-2, on main. Per records_import.rs, the branch was filled by a one-time import. If a newer role version exists only on main, the page uses an older limit; if none was imported, it treats the role as undefined and lists everything. That fails toward showing more, which is the safer direction. The same reading of the branch already existed for the recommendation line, so this predates the change, but the new filter now depends on it. A simpler, more correct option is to read records/roles from main's tree too, as the base already does for work decisions.

findings.summary: docs/design/explainer-site.md still describes the page as the Steward's 'open proposals'.
findings.evidence: This is not wrong, only less precise than the new above-limit rule. docs/architecture.md was optional and was left unchanged.

summary: The change does what was asked. The decisions page now lists only open proposals whose rung is above the raising role's limit, using the same rule as athena-core's in_limit, and with none it shows one line, "Nothing waiting for you". The missing-branch message "No proposals listed" stays separate. Three new tests build pages through locate() and render() on temp git repos and check the cards, the "1 waiting" heading and the empty state; all 15 decisions tests passed when I ran `cargo test -p xtask decisions`. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed. I checked the changelog against the evidence snapshot: the three decisions are on main, 3b1f8c1 landed on 4 Nov, ne91 is never called undecided, and no workflow change is proposed. No base-run output was given to me, so I judged criterion 4 from the base code in the diff: the base has no limit filter, so the within-limit tests fail there. There are three minor findings, none blocking. First, a new test comment (following the reading's criterion 3) says approve-work writes to the records branch; the code shows it writes to main, like reject-work. Second, a comment and the changelog say only the within-limit assertions fail on the base, but the new empty-state wording assertions would fail there too. Third, the filter reads role limits only from the records branch, a pre-existing design that fails toward showing more proposals. All changed files are within the expected deliverables.
